title: Genuine capability gap — Program Manager with no personal product-decision ownership

assessment.general_capability: Product management ownership — personally owning product strategy, roadmap, and final feature/launch calls.
assessment.target_specific_requirement: Senior PM Consumer Product — personal ownership of product strategy and final product calls for consumer features at Senior scope.

seed_gap.gap_title: No evidence of personal product management ownership
seed_gap.gap_description: Resume shows strong program management execution but no personal ownership of product decisions, strategy, or prioritization. Target role requires owning product strategy and making final product calls.
seed_gap.recommended_fix: Establish whether the candidate has owned any product decisions directly.

seed_analysis.positioning_summary: Strong Technical Program Manager profile. For a Senior PM target, the central question is whether the candidate has personally owned product decisions beyond coordinating others' decisions.

related_signals.rationale: Strong track record of release and dependency management.

persona.fallback_answer: That falls outside my ownership — the PMs on the team owned product decisions. I owned execution.

answer_rules.answer: Honestly, I don't own product decisions. The PMs on the teams I supported owned the roadmap, prioritization, and strategic calls. I own schedules, dependencies, and risks.

I don't have an example of personally making a product decision. The closest thing would be when I pushed back on a timeline because a dependency was slipping, but the scope and feature calls were the PM's.
I coordinate a 40-person platform organization across 6 engineering teams. 12 major releases over the last two years at a 95% on-time rate.
95% on-time release rate, a 40% drop in cross-team dependency slips, and 2x faster quarterly planning cycles. Those are execution outcomes though — not product outcomes.
I'll be straightforward — I haven't done the product-ownership work this role requires. I've been adjacent to it as a TPM, but I haven't owned a product's strategy, roadmap, or launch calls myself.

forbidden_claims: senior pm with strong product ownership
